title: Launch Pad Lite — task-driven template cards + glance-help rail for first-run console
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: New users land on the console with an intimidating surface of dashboards, rollout controls, and cost charts. Existing empty-state patterns are long-form and interruptive; engineers want quick, actionable entry points that guide them to value without blocking.

Goal: Design a compact "Launch Pad Lite" surface that sits on empty dashboards and newly created projects, combining a set of task-driven template cards (micro-scenarios such as 'Run a quick generation', 'Try cost estimator', 'Create embedding index') with a persistent glance-help rail: a thin, dismissible strip that surfaces contextual hints, cost micro-education, and one-click templates. Aim for low cognitive load, fast discoverability, and measurable conversion to first-successful-inference.

Success metrics (proposal):
- 20% lift in 'first inference' conversion from new project creation within 7 days.
- 30% reduction in time-to-first-PR for integrations when templates are used.
- 15% increased interaction with cost literacy tips on first 3 sessions.

Design components and behaviour:
- Template cards: 3–4 compact cards stacked horizontally (mobile collapses to a carousel). Each card includes a short scenario, estimated cost tier badge, and a one-click 'Try in sandbox' button that provisions a temporary demo project. Cards should be data-driven: surface recommended templates based on detected account signals (e.g., embedding-heavy usage surfaces 'Create embedding index').
- Glance-help rail: 48px high rail that appears on the right edge of dashboards and can expand to a 240px panel on hover/click. Rail items are micro-tips (10–20 words) with an icon and optional CTA. Tip types: Quickstart, Cost Tip, Rollout Best Practice, Troubleshooting. Rail state persists per-user with an analytics event for dismiss/expand.
- Empty-state composition: combine Launch Pad Lite with an action-focused primary CTA and a secondary 'Explore templates' link. Keep content density low; provide 'Learn more' links to modal walkthroughs and template detail pages.

Accessibility & localization considerations:
- Ensure rail expand/collapse is keyboard navigable and has ARIA roles.
- Template cards must be readable at 14px, sufficient color contrast for badges, and support screen-reader labels for cost badges.
- Copy should be locale-agnostic; leave room for translation expansion.

Analytics/events to instrument:
- launchpad_shown (context: project_id, user_id, placement)
- template_clicked (template_id, action_source)
- sandbox_provisioned (template_id, success)
- glance_help_expanded / glance_help_dismissed
- cost_tip_cta_clicked

Trade-offs discussed:
- Prefetching demo sandboxes increases friction/cost on the infra side; proposal uses on-demand provisioning but caches lightweight sandbox state for 3 hours.
- Personalization requires onboarding signals; to start we use simple heuristics (account plan, prior API calls) and gather event data for a later ML-enriched recommendation layer.

Prototype links and artifacts: see comments for Figma flows, clickthrough prototype, and PRD draft.

Next steps: finalize copy, hand off to frontend for an experimental rollout behind a feature flag, instrument analytics, and run a 2-week pilot for newly-created projects with A/B allocation (25% treatment).
